title: Fossil horse skulls match interpolated stages between Hyracotherium and Equus

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Fossil horse skulls match interpolated stages between Hyracotherium and Equus

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Skulls interpolated by coordinate transformation between Hyracotherium (Eohippus) and Equus coincide closely with actual fossil skulls of Mesohippus and Protohippus, which therefore lie on the transformation series from Eohippus to the horse.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XVII: On the Theory of Transformations, or the Comparison of Related Forms

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: it will be seen that the actual fossil skull coincides in the most perfect fashion with one of the hypothetical forms or stages which our method shews to be implicitly involved in the transition from _Hyracotherium_ to _Equus_.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XVII, “On the Theory of Transformations, or the Comparison of Related Forms”; topic “Interpolated intermediates in horse evolution”. Scope: skulls of fossil and living Equidae

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch17-14: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.81

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Geometric coincidence has a clear quantitative test and relevant fossils are available digitally. Prespecification and null comparisons avoid a largely visual, post hoc match and make the analysis discriminating.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fit a prespecified transformation between Hyracotherium and Equus skulls, generate interpolated surfaces, and measure their blinded geometric distance to Mesohippus and Protohippus versus other equid fossils and null morphospaces.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Interpolation can be tuned unless fixed before examining intermediates.

Fossil completeness and deformation vary.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The interpolation test is well defined and the taxa are classical, with published measurements and a growing set of scans. Open 3D coverage of Mesohippus, Protohippus and Hyracotherium is incomplete, so a team would still compile plates and specimens. The geometric coincidence can be assessed for the available skulls and does not by itself prove the phylogenetic series.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Build a coordinate path from Hyracotherium to Equus and measure the distance of Mesohippus and Protohippus skulls to the interpolated shapes, relative to skulls that are not on that path. Close coincidence, closer than off-path equids, would support the claim; distances as large as those of unrelated perissodactyls would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Complete, undistorted skulls of the named fossil genera are few, and only some are openly scanned.

A linear morph between two endpoints can pass near intermediate fossils without those fossils lying on the phylogenetic path.
